title: CLEAN_ROOM_HANDOFF_FACTS.json
description: A strict, mechanically-checkable 'facts only' handoff format -- the common case for protocol/schema clean-room work (wire-format field/enum enumeration) where a handoff document should contain bare facts (names, numbers, types) and nothing else: no prose, no commentary, no structure leaked verbatim from Zone R. This is an ADDITIONAL, stricter option alongside the free-form Markdown handoff (CLEAN_ROOM_HANDOFF.md) produced by 'cleanroom handoff' -- it does not replace it, and is not a fit for clean-room work that genuinely needs prose (e.g. behavioural/algorithmic specifications). Every string field is deliberately short and identifier-shaped (no newlines, small max lengths) so that a document trying to smuggle a paragraph of copied commentary through as a 'name' or 'notes' value fails schema validation rather than relying purely on an analyst's judgement. NOTE per this project's CONTRIBUTING.md/GOVERNANCE.md: this file lives under schemas/ and requires human legal/governance review beyond a passing test run, same as every other schema in this directory.

source_note.description: Optional short, non-prose provenance label (e.g. 'meshtastic mesh.proto v2.6'). Not a place for commentary.

kind.description: What sort of bare fact this is. Intentionally a closed, small set -- a new kind of fact is a schema change (human-reviewed), not a free-text tag.

container.description: The enclosing enum/message/service name, e.g. 'HardwareModel' or 'EnvironmentMetrics'.

value.description: A bare scalar value (e.g. an enum's numeric value). If a string, it must still satisfy short_type_expr-like brevity -- validated additionally by the facts-json handoff validator beyond what JSON Schema alone can express.

notes.description: An optional short, single-line annotation -- never a place for copied prose or commentary. Long or multi-line content belongs in a free-form Markdown handoff instead, not here.
